# Platform card: Google Antigravity

Last verified: 2026-10-23. Versions checked: App 2.0.10, IDE 2.5.5, CLI `agy` 1.4.5.

Antigravity moves fast. When a detail matters and may be stale, ask the `platform-researcher` agent to re-check it.

Primary sources:
- antigravity.google/docs (skills, rules, subagents, plugins, hooks, cli/gcli-migration, migration/workflows-to-skills);
- github.com/google-antigravity/antigravity-cli (CHANGELOG.md);
- the IDE's built-in `agy-customizations` skill docs.

## Contents
1. Surfaces and roots
2. Instructions and rules
3. Skills
4. Agents
5. Tools and model tiers

## 1. Surfaces and roots
- **Surfaces:**
  - **App** (2.x desktop);
  - **IDE** (VS Code fork; the 2.5.x line has had no releases since 2026-08-13);
  - **CLI `agy`** (Go, closed source, near-daily releases);
  - extensions for VS Code and Visual Studio.

  All share one harness, but subagents are documented only for the App and the CLI.
- **Workspace root:** `.agents/`, discovered by walking up to the repo root. Legacy names `.agent/`, `_agents/` and `_agent/` still work.
- **Workspace boundaries for execution:** in the Antigravity runtime, `run_command` requires `Cwd` to be located within an active workspace folder. When working on an external target repository, add the target folder to the workspace (as a multi-root workspace in Antigravity IDE) or run commands directly from the target folder via `agy -p`.
- **Global root:** `~/.gemini/config/`, shared by App, IDE and CLI.
  - Antigravity 1.x used `~/.gemini/antigravity/`, which old codelabs still show.
  - Some CLI docs also list `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/{skills,plugins,rules}`. The two sources conflict; prefer `~/.gemini/config/` and verify on the installed version.
- **Precedence, high to low:**
  1. workspace
  2. paths declared in `skills.json` / `plugins.json`
  3. `~/.gemini/config/`
  4. built-ins
  5. global declared paths

  The higher entry wins a name clash.
- **Manifests:** `skills.json`, `rules.json`, `agents.json`, `plugins.json` (in `.agents/` or the global root):
  - Shape: `{"inherits":[…], "entries":[{"path", "include_only", "exclude"}]}`.
  - Entries are scanned flat; name nested items in `include_only`.

## 2. Instructions and rules
- **Always-on files** (no frontmatter), loaded at every directory level from the edited file up to the root: `AGENTS.md` or `GEMINI.md`, `.agents/AGENTS.md` or `.agents/GEMINI.md`.
- **Global files:**
  - `~/.gemini/{AGENTS,GEMINI}.md`;
  - `~/.gemini/config/{AGENTS,GEMINI}.md`;
  - `~/.gemini/config/rules/*.md`.
- **Rules:** `.agents/rules/*.md` (scanned flat; nested files must be listed in `rules.json`). Frontmatter:

  | `trigger` | Required extra field | Behavior |
  |---|---|---|
  | `always_on` | — | always injected |
  | `model_decision` | `description` | path + description injected; content read on demand |
  | `glob` | `globs` (or `glob`), comma-separated | loaded for matching files |
  | `manual` | — | loaded on `@`-mention |

  An invalid trigger (for example `alwaysOn`) is **silently discarded**.
- **Limits:**
  - 24 KB per rule file;
  - a shared **20,000-token** budget for global + always-on rules. Over budget, the largest files are demoted to one-line pointers.
- **Imports:** `@path` references work in AGENTS.md and rules (App 2.11+).
- **Workflows:** `.agents/workflows/` and `global_workflows/` **stopped working on 2026-10-19**. Skills replace them; `/migrate-workflows` converts old ones.

## 3. Skills
- **Locations:**
  - workspace `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (legacy `.agent/skills/`);
  - global `~/.gemini/config/skills/<name>/`;
  - plugin `plugins/<p>/skills/<name>/`.
- **Frontmatter:**
  - `name`: optional, defaults to the folder name, lowercase-hyphen.
  - `description`: required; third person, says what and when.
  - Extras:
    - `disable-slash-command: true` (CLI 1.1.12+): hidden from the `/` menu, the model can still use it;
    - `metadata.icon` (an emoji).

  Unknown keys are tolerated. Keep to the Agent Skills standard fields plus these extras.
- **Folders:** `scripts/`, `references/`, `examples/`, `resources/`.
  - Link bundled files with relative paths from SKILL.md.
  - The docs suggest running scripts with `--help` rather than reading their source.
- **Invocation:**
  - The model sees name + description and reads SKILL.md when relevant.
  - Every skill is also a slash command: `/name`, or `/<plugin>:<skill>` for plugin skills. Commands can be stacked (`/plan /grill …`).
  - In the IDE, skills appear in the Customizations menu.
- **Loading another skill from a skill:** tell the agent explicitly to invoke `/<skill>` or to read that skill's SKILL.md by path. Naming it in prose is not reliable.
- **Limits:** `agy plugin validate` warns on a body over **24 KB**, on name/folder mismatch, and on duplicate names.
- **Reload:** `/skills reload` (CLI).

## 4. Agents (custom subagents)
- **Surfaces:** App and CLI. The IDE is not documented.
- **Locations:**
  - workspace `.agents/agents/<name>.md` or `.agents/agents/<name>/agent.md`;
  - global `~/.gemini/config/agents/…`;
  - plugin `plugins/<p>/agents/`.

  `agent.json` files are ignored; agents are Markdown with YAML frontmatter.
- **Frontmatter:**

  | Field | Type / default | Notes |
  |---|---|---|
  | `name` | string, required | unique |
  | `description` | string, required | the planner uses it to decide when to delegate |
  | `tools` | string[], default `[]` | exact tool names (section 5); **a misspelled or unknown name can hang the agent** |
  | `model` | `inherit` (default), `flash`, `pro` | |
  | `commandExecutionPolicy` | `off`, `auto`, `eager`, `sandbox` (default) | |
  | `mainAgent` | bool, default `true` | selectable as the primary agent |
  | `subagent` | bool, default `true` | invocable via `invoke_subagent` |
  | `skills`, `plugins` | string[] of paths (relative to the agent file) | knowledge to load |
  | `mcpServers` | object[] | |
  | `hidden`, `inheritMcp`, `inheritCustomizations`, `rules`, `agents`, `excludeDefaultComponents`, `hooks` | from CLI/App changelogs | Since CLI 1.1.25 agents inherit ambient skills, rules and subagents by default |

- **Body:** the system prompt, in Markdown. Google's example uses `# System Prompt` and `# Review Guidelines` headings.
- **Invocation:**
  - `invoke_subagent` (planner or explicit);
  - `@<agent> message` (CLI 1.2.9+);
  - `agy --agent <name>` (as main agent);
  - the `/agents` panel;
  - in the App, subagent cards.
- **Built-ins:** `research` (codebase exploration), `browser` (`/browser` only), `self` (a clone of the caller), `image-generator`.
- **Limits:**
  - nesting is capped at 10 levels;
  - subagents inherit the parent's command prefixes, file scopes and sandbox settings.
- **Transient agents:** `define_subagent` creates one at runtime.

## 5. Tools and model tiers

**Tool names.** Use only these in `tools:`.

| Capability | Antigravity tool | Status |
|---|---|---|
| read file | `view_file` | documented |
| file outline / symbol | `view_file_outline`, `view_code_item` | seen in IDE 2.5.5 binary |
| edit file | `replace_file_content`, `multi_replace_file_content` | documented |
| create file | `write_to_file` | documented |
| list / find files | `list_dir`, `find_by_name` | documented |
| search text | `grep_search` | documented |
| semantic search | `codebase_search` | binary |
| run command | `run_command` | documented (requires Cwd in workspace) |
| command follow-up | `command_status`, `send_command_input`, `read_terminal` | binary |
| web | `search_web`, `read_url_content` | documented |
| delegate | `invoke_subagent` (+ `define_subagent`) | documented |
| browser | `browser_subagent` | binary |

"Binary" means the identifier appears in the shipped language-server binary. It is probably a tool name, but confirm it before relying on it (use `platform-researcher` or a quick test agent).

| Abstract tier | Antigravity value |
|---|---|
| same as caller | `inherit` |
| fast / cheap | `flash` |
| strongest | `pro` |

## 6. Plugins, hooks, MCP
- **Plugin layout** (in a customization root, `.agents/plugins/` or `~/.gemini/config/plugins/`):
  ```
  plugins/<name>/
  ├── plugin.json
  ├── skills/<skill>/SKILL.md
  ├── agents/<agent>.md        (App/CLI)
  ├── rules/*.md
  ├── hooks.json
  └── mcp_config.json
  ```
- **`plugin.json` manifest:**
  - IDE docs: only `name` (optional).
  - CLI: requires `name` (`^[a-zA-Z0-9-_]+$`) and `description`, and rejects unknown keys.
  - Since CLI 1.3.2 the manifest may sit in `.antigravity-plugin/` or `.gemini-plugin/`.
  - `version` is accepted (checked with `agy plugin validate` on CLI 1.4.5; an unknown key only warns).
  - Keep to `name`, `description` and `version` unless you verified more fields.
- **Behavior:** plugin skills and tools are namespaced (`/<plugin>:<skill>`). Plugins load `commands/` and `workflows/` **not at all**.
- **Install:**
  - drop the folder into a plugins root (workspace `.agents/plugins/` or global `~/.gemini/config/plugins/`);
  - or `agy plugin install <path | https://github.com/o/r[/tree/main/subdir]>` (installs globally into `~/.gemini/config/plugins/<name>`);
  - or for workspace isolation without modifying global configuration, link into `<target>/.agents/plugins/<name>` (via `uv run tools/install.py antigravity --scope workspace` or directory junction);
  - or the official marketplace `antigravity-plugins-official`.

  Check with `agy plugin validate <dir>` and `agy plugin list --json`.
- **Hooks:** `.agents/hooks.json`, a global one, or the plugin's `hooks.json`.
  - Events: `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PreInvocation`, `PostInvocation`, `Stop`.
  - Tool events take regex matchers.
- **MCP:** `mcp_config.json` (global `~/.gemini/config/`, workspace `.agents/`, or plugin):
  - `{"mcpServers": {"x": {"command", "args", "env"} | {"serverUrl", "headers"}}}`.
  - Plugin servers are namespaced `<plugin>_<server>`.

## 7. Testing
- **List what loaded:** `agy -p "/skills" --output-format json` lists standalone skills without an agent turn (CI-friendly). It does **not** list plugin skills (`/<plugin>:<skill>`), and `agy plugin list` shows only global installs (checked on agy 1.4.6). To check a workspace plugin, run `agy plugin validate <plugin folder>` and invoke one of its skills.
- **Workspace from the CLI:** `agy --add-dir <path>` (repeatable) adds a folder to the workspace, so `run_command` may use it.
- **Headless behavior run:** `agy -p "<prompt>" --output-format json`. Inspect the output for skill activation or `invoke_subagent` calls. Exact output fields: verify on the installed version.
- **Interactive:** `/skills reload`, `/agents`, `@agent`.
- **Validation:** `agy plugin validate`. It warns on missing frontmatter, name/folder mismatch, body > 24 KB, duplicate names, and Claude-style `commands/` or top-level `"hooks"`.
- **Evals:** there is no official eval runner. Use the stablehand eval protocol with a `scenario-runner` subagent and `agy -p` runs.

## 8. Gotchas
- Before CLI 1.3.6, an unquoted `description:` containing a colon broke loading of skills, rules and agents. Always double-quote frontmatter strings.
- An invalid rule `trigger` is dropped silently, and an unknown tool name in an agent can hang it. Lint before use.
- `.agents/skills/` is also read by OpenCode. Keep Antigravity-tailored skills in a workspace plugin (`.agents/plugins/<set>/skills/`) when the repo is also used with OpenCode (see `coexistence.md`).
- Google's own built-in skills are loose: underscores in folder names, missing frontmatter. Don't copy that style; follow the Agent Skills standard.
- Claude Code plugins are not consumed as-is: there are no `commands/`, and the hooks file sits at a different path.
